newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bad vodka killes nine in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Bad vodka killes nine in Russia.

text.p: Nine people have died and 10 were fighting for their lives in the Russian town of Shchuchye after drinking tainted vodka, police said on Saturday.
A duty officer in the regional centre of Kurgan said by telephone the poisoning took place on Friday and four women were among the dead.

The average age of the victims, all of whom had drunk the brew poisoned with methylated spirit, was about 30 years, he said. Shchuchye is about 200 km (130 miles) east of Kurgan, in the southern Urals.
Earlier this month 22 people died in the Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk after drinking tainted vodka.
The number of alcohol-related deaths in Russia has more than doubled during the 1990s as many vendors have offered cheap moonshine to a public eager for bargains.
President Boris Yeltsin has launched a campaign aimed at restoring at least partial state monopoly of the alcohol market.
Vladimir Yarmosh, the head of Russia's powerful alcohol producers' lobby Spirtprom, has said fake vodka poisoning claims between 50,000 and 100,000 Russians lives a year.

Yarmosh's figures are higher than official ones which show that alcohol poisoning accounted for almost 23 deaths per every 100,000 Russians in 1996 or about 35,000 people a year. But even the official rate is twice as high as it was in 1990.
